research_rationale:
EO 11298 (signed 1966-08-14; 31 FR 10915) is a single paragraph in which the President prescribes, under 10 U.S.C. 1035 as amended by the Act of August 14, 1966, ten percent per annum, compounded quarterly, as the interest rate on amounts deposited by members of the uniformed services, and states that the order is effective September 1, 1966. I read the complete held Federal Register text. The dossier inventory of one clause covers the whole order and I confirmed it without correction. The effective-date sentence fixes a start, not an end, and no sunset or ending condition appears. A search of the held texts for the order's number finds only the order's own Federal Register page and the 1989 codification entry, which lists no amendment or revocation. The three bounded machine searches record no adverse disposition. The clause is therefore treated as operative on the original text through 2026-10-14. Whether the statute still authorizes the rate was not read from held statute text; that is a limit of the bounded-search basis and is not claimed as quoted authority.

research_rationale:
EO 12598 (signed 1987-06-17; 52 FR 23421) implements Title VIII of the Omnibus Diplomatic Security and Antiterrorism Act of 1986 (Public Law 99-399). Sections 1 and 2 delegate presidential functions under section 803(a) to the Secretary of State (section 2 in consultation with the Secretary of Labor); sections 3 and 4 delegate functions under section 806 to the Secretary of Defense (section 4 in consultation with the Secretary of Labor); section 5 directs the Secretaries of State and Defense to consult with each other and other agencies; section 6 supersedes Executive Order No. 12576. I read the complete held Federal Register text. The dossier inventory of six clauses, one per section, covers the whole order and I confirmed it without correction. No section has a fixed end. Section 6 acts on another instrument and was performed on issuance, so I record it as spent on the order's date; its own effect on EO 12576 survives in that order's absence. A search of the held texts for the number finds only the order's own page and the 1989 codification entry, which lists no amendment or revocation, and the three bounded machine searches record no adverse disposition. Sections 1 to 5 are therefore operative on the original text through 2026-10-14. The statute and CFR text the searches point to are not held as quoted text and are not relied on as authority.

Executive Order 10864
DESIGNATING THE PAN AMERICAN  
HEALTH ORGANIZATION AS A  
PUBLIC INTERNATIONAL ORGANI­
ZATION ENTITLED TO ENJOY CER­
TAIN PRIVILEGES, EXEMPTIONS,  
AND IMMUNITIES
By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by section 1  of the International Organi­
zations Immunities Act, approved De­
cember 29, 1945 (59 Stat. 669), and 
having found that the United States 
participates in the Pan American Health 
Organization pursuant to the authority 
of the Pan American Sanitary Conven­
tion ratified by the President on March 
28, 1925, with the advice and consent of 
the Senate given on February 23, 1925 
(44 Stat. 2031, TS 714), I hereby desig­
nate the Pan American Health Organi­
zation as a public international organi­
zation entitled to enjoy the privileges, 
exemptions, and immunities conferred 
by the International Organizations Im­
munities Act.
The designation of the Pan American 
Health Organization as a public inter­
national organization within the mean­
ing of the International Organizations 
Immunities Act is not intended to 
abridge in any respect privileges, ex­
emptions, arid immunities which that 
organization may have acquired or may 
acquire by treaty or congressional action.
The designation of the Pan American 
Health Organization made by this order 
shall be deemed to include the designa­
tion of the Pan American Sanitary 
Bureau. The designation of the Pan 
American Sanitary Bureau made by 
Executive Order No. 9751 of July 11, 
1946, is hereby superseded, and that 
order is amended accordingly.
Dwight  D. E isenhower

research_rationale:
EO 10863 (signed 1960-02-18; 25 FR 1507) designates the Attorney General, under section 1 of Title VI of the act of June 15, 1917 as amended (22 U.S.C. 401), as the person authorized to seize and detain arms and munitions of war, other articles and vessels, vehicles or aircraft used in illegal export (section 1), and lets any officer of the Department of Justice designated by the Attorney General exercise that authority (section 2). I read the complete held Federal Register text; the held file also reprints the next order on the page (EO 10864), which is not part of this order and is the only reason the number appears in a second held file. The dossier inventory is one clause spanning sections 1 and 2; I confirmed that it covers every command of the order. The order has no sunset or ending condition. A search of the held texts for the number finds no other instrument that cites it apart from that page overlap and the 1989 codification entry, which lists no amendment or revocation, and the three bounded machine searches record no adverse disposition. The clause is operative on the original text through 2026-10-14. The statute and CFR text the searches point to are not held as quoted text and are not relied on as authority.

savings_residuals.reason: The order has no savings, transition or accrued-rights clause and nothing held ends it, so no residual effect arises.
